title: Plants: Anatomy, Growth and Function
seo_title: Grade 11 Biology (SBI3U): Plants: Anatomy, Growth and Function Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Plant tissues (dermal, ground, vascular) and organs (roots, stems, leaves); transport of water and sugars in xylem and phloem; photosynthesis and the factors that affect it; and plant growth, hormones and responses. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Biology, Grade 11, University Preparation (SBI3U), Strand F: Plants: Anatomy, Growth, and Function)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Biology (SBI3U) worksheets on plants: plant tissues, roots, stems and leaves, xylem and phloem, transpiration, photosynthesis and plant hormones. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Xylem carries water up; phloem carries sugars to where they are used.
key_sub: Leaves are built for photosynthesis; stomata control gas exchange and water loss.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants have three tissue systems: dermal (epidermis, guard cells, root hairs), ground (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) and vascular (xylem and phloem). Meristems at root and shoot tips make new cells for growth.

Water enters root hairs by osmosis and is pulled up the xylem by transpiration from the leaves. Sugars made in photosynthesis move in the phloem from sources (leaves) to sinks (roots, fruits). Hormones such as auxin, gibberellin and abscisic acid control growth and responses like phototropism.

Example

On a hot, windy day, what happens to the rate of transpiration?

More evaporation from the leaves

Answer: it increases

Example

Which hormone makes a shoot bend towards light?

Cells on the shaded side grow longer.

Answer: auxin

Common mistakes

  • Saying xylem carries sugars: xylem carries water and minerals.
  • Thinking plants take in food from the soil: they make sugars by photosynthesis.
  • Forgetting that stomata close to save water, which also slows photosynthesis.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support?
items.e: Sclerenchyma: dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support.

items.q: What is the periderm made of?
items.e: It replaces the epidermis in older stems.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis?
items.e: Parenchyma: thin-walled living cells used for storage and photosynthesis.

items.q: What is endarch xylem?
c: protoxylem towards the centre and metaxylem towards the outside
items.e: Found in stems; roots are exarch.

items.q: Which description fits collenchyma?
c: living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
conducting water and minerals from roots
items.e: Collenchyma: living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as cells that open and close the stomatal pore?
items.e: Guard cells: cells that open and close the stomatal pore.

items.q: Which cell has many mitochondria, giving more energy released by respiration for contraction?
items.e: Each specialized cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as cork, the dead outer layer of bark?
items.e: Phellem: cork, the dead outer layer of bark.

items.q: A red blood cell has no nucleus and a biconcave shape. How does this help it?
c: many proteins made and packaged for secretion
an empty, continuous tube that carries water and gives support
energy to swim to the egg
more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots?
items.e: Pericycle: the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots.

items.q: What is a dorsiventral leaf?
c: a leaf with the same tissue on both sides
a leaf with palisade on the upper side and spongy tissue below, as in dicots
items.e: Isobilateral leaves (grasses) differ.

items.q: A muscle cell has many mitochondria. How does this help it?
c: more energy released by respiration for contraction
a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
many proteins made and packaged for secretion
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems?
items.e: Hypodermis: the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems.

items.q: A root hair cell has a long, narrow extension. How does this help it?
c: a larger surface area to absorb water and mineral salts
energy to swim to the egg
a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: A sperm cell has a tail (flagellum) and many mitochondria. How does this help it?
c: many proteins made and packaged for secretion
an empty, continuous tube that carries water and gives support
a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
energy to swim to the egg
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: What is the function of the pericycle in roots?
c: it gives rise to lateral roots
items.e: It lies just inside the endodermis.

items.q: A guard cell has a thicker inner wall. How does this help it?
c: more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen
a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
an empty, continuous tube that carries water and gives support
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as conducting water and minerals from roots?
items.e: Xylem: conducting water and minerals from roots.

items.q: Which cells guard the stomata of grasses?
items.e: Dicots have bean-shaped guard cells.

items.q: What does the vascular cambium produce?
c: secondary xylem on the inside and secondary phloem on the outside
items.e: This causes growth in girth.

items.q: Which description fits phellem?
c: conducting water and minerals from roots
the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots
cork, the dead outer layer of bark
items.e: Phellem: cork, the dead outer layer of bark.

items.q: Which description fits xylem?
c: the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex
specialized parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes
dead cells with thick lignified walls that give mechanical support
conducting water and minerals from roots
items.e: Xylem: conducting water and minerals from roots.

items.q: Which description fits a dicot root?
c: radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith
vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium
radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith
scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath
items.e: Dicot root: radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith.

items.q: Which description fits a monocot stem?
c: radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith
vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium
radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith
scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath
items.e: Monocot stem: scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath.

items.q: What is phyllotaxy?
c: the pattern in which leaves are arranged on a stem
items.e: Alternate, opposite or whorled.

items.q: Which is a parthenocarpic fruit?
items.e: It develops without fertilization.

items.q: Which description fits hypodermis?
c: conducting water and minerals from roots
the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems
cells that open and close the stomatal pore
the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex
items.e: Hypodermis: the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems.

items.q: What is the outer covering of the seed of maize that is fused with the fruit wall?
c: the seed coat fused with pericarp (a caryopsis grain)
items.e: Maize grain is a fruit.

items.q: Which phyllotaxy does Alstonia have?
items.e: More than two leaves at each node.

items.q: What is sapwood?
c: the light-coloured outer wood that still conducts water
items.e: Also called alburnum.

items.q: In which organ is this seen: scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath?
items.e: Monocot stem: scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath.

items.q: Which description fits pericycle?
c: the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots
a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss
the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots
living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
items.e: Pericycle: the layer just inside the endodermis that gives rise to lateral roots.

items.q: Which description fits spongy parenchyma?
c: specialized parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes
loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
cells that open and close the stomatal pore
conducting water and minerals from roots
items.e: Spongy parenchyma: loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf.

items.q: Which plant has a fibrous root system?
items.e: Monocots like wheat have fibrous roots.

items.q: In which organ is this seen: radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith?
items.e: Monocot root: radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith.

items.q: Which description fits a dicot stem?
c: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium
radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith
radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith
scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath
items.e: Dicot stem: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis?
items.e: Palisade parenchyma: tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis.

items.q: What is the cotyledon of a grass seed called?
items.e: It is a single large shield-shaped cotyledon.

items.q: In which organ is this seen: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium?
items.e: Dicot stem: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium.

items.q: Which description fits a monocot root?
c: scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath
radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith
radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith
vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium
items.e: Monocot root: radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith.

items.q: In 2 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 18 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.75 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 0.75² × 18 = 31.8 mm³; ÷ 2 min = 15.9 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: What is the effect of windy conditions on the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Transpiration is faster when the air is warm, dry and moving and the stomata are open in light.

items.q: What is the effect of lower temperature on the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Transpiration is faster when the air is warm, dry and moving and the stomata are open in light.

items.q: In a potometer, the air bubble moves 5 cm along the tube in 4 minutes. What is the rate of water uptake in cm per minute?
items.e: Rate = distance ÷ time = 5 ÷ 4.

items.q: What is the effect of darkness (stomata close) on the rate of transpiration?

items.q: In 10 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 30 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.60 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 0.60² × 30 = 33.9 mm³; ÷ 10 min = 3.39 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: Why does high humidity reduce transpiration?
c: the water potential gradient between the leaf and the air is smaller
items.e: Less water vapour diffuses out.

items.q: What is the effect of higher temperature on the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Transpiration is faster when the air is warm, dry and moving and the stomata are open in light.

items.q: What is the effect of higher humidity on the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Transpiration is faster when the air is warm, dry and moving and the stomata are open in light.

items.q: In 2 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 50 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.60 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 0.60² × 50 = 56.5 mm³; ÷ 2 min = 28.3 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: What forms the xylem?
c: dead cells with no end walls, forming continuous tubes
items.e: The tubes are strengthened by lignin.

items.q: In 10 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 15 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.60 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 0.60² × 15 = 17.0 mm³; ÷ 10 min = 1.70 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: A plant in a greenhouse at 5 °C on a sunny winter day with extra carbon dioxide photosynthesizes slowly. What is the limiting factor?
items.e: The limiting factor is the one that, when increased, increases the rate.

items.q: A water plant gives off 18 bubbles of oxygen in 3 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis in bubbles per minute?
items.e: Rate = 18 ÷ 3. Counting bubbles measures the oxygen released.

items.q: What is ethephon used for in agriculture?
c: hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple
increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems
items.e: Ethephon: hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple.

items.q: Which hormone is found in coconut milk and maize kernels?
items.e: Kinetin was first found in autoclaved herring sperm DNA.

items.q: What is photoperiodism?
c: the response of plants to the relative lengths of day and night
items.e: It controls flowering.

items.q: What is GA₃ used for in agriculture?
c: hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple
increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems
items.e: GA₃: increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems.

items.q: Which plant hormone causes cell division and delaying leaf senescence?
items.e: Cytokinin: cell division and delaying leaf senescence.

items.q: Which effect is caused by abscisic acid?
c: cell division and delaying leaf senescence
stem elongation and bolting in cabbage
closing stomata and seed dormancy (the stress hormone)
apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings
items.e: Abscisic acid: closing stomata and seed dormancy (the stress hormone).

items.q: What is heterophylly?
c: different shapes of leaves on the same plant
the same leaf in all plants
items.e: e.g. buttercup in water and in air.

items.q: Which hormone is called the stress hormone?
items.e: It helps plants survive drought.

items.q: What is 2,4-D used for in agriculture?
c: increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems
hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple
items.e: 2,4-D: killing broad-leaved weeds.

items.q: Which chemical is used for increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems?
items.e: GA₃: increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems.

items.q: Which hormone causes bolting in cabbage?
items.e: Bolting is rapid stem growth before flowering.

items.q: Which effect is caused by gibberellin?
c: apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings
closing stomata and seed dormancy (the stress hormone)
stem elongation and bolting in cabbage
items.e: Gibberellin: stem elongation and bolting in cabbage.

items.q: What is NAA used for in agriculture?
c: hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple
increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems
items.e: NAA: rooting of stem cuttings.

items.q: What is apical dominance?
c: the growing shoot tip stops lateral buds from growing
items.e: Removing the tip (as in tea plants) gives a bushy plant.

items.q: Which hormone is a gas?
items.e: It speeds ripening.

items.q: What is vernalization?
c: promotion of flowering by a period of low temperature
items.e: e.g. winter wheat and biennials.

items.q: Which plant hormone causes fruit ripening and leaf fall?
items.e: Ethylene: fruit ripening and leaf fall.

items.q: Which effect is caused by cytokinin?
c: cell division and delaying leaf senescence
stem elongation and bolting in cabbage
closing stomata and seed dormancy (the stress hormone)
items.e: Cytokinin: cell division and delaying leaf senescence.

items.q: Which effect is caused by ethene?
c: closing stomata and seed dormancy (the stress hormone)
stem elongation and bolting in cabbage
cell division and delaying leaf senescence
items.e: Ethylene: fruit ripening and leaf fall.

items.q: Which plant hormone causes apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings?
items.e: Auxin: apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings.
